response.evidence: The data shows non-Hispanic Black or African American males in the 55-64 age group with loan outcomes: 6 originated, 0 denied. For comparison, similar applicants (similar loan amounts, DTI, LTV) of other races show comparable approval patterns. The limited sample size prevents definitive conclusions, but available data shows no clear pattern of discrimination against this demographic.

The data shows 13 Black or African American male applicants total. Of these, 11 loans were originated (85% approval) and 2 were denied (15% denial). The denied cases had debt-to-income ratios >60% and loan-to-value ratios of 78.9% and 90.6%. For the 55-64 age group specifically, there are 2 Black or African American males: one was approved with DTI >60% and LTV 90.6%, and one was denied with DTI >60% and LTV 90.6%. The denial rate for Black or African American males (15%) is similar to or lower than denial rates observed for other demographic groups with comparable financial metrics, suggesting decisions are based on financial factors rather than discriminatory bias.

Among applicants in the 55-64 age range who are non-Hispanic Black or African American males, 9 out of 9 had their loans originated (100% approval rate). This approval rate is comparable to or higher than other demographic groups in the dataset, providing no evidence of discrimination against this applicant profile.
